answer: Each submission hangs on the atlas of a task receipt, and the knoll is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The echo of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts split across independent auditors. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a concise reports, one example per claim register, it stays short.
